I'm looking at the Nxeon platform's admin "Failed jobs" dashboard (repo at /opt/nxeon). I see a recurring pattern of FAILED jobs (each exhausted 3 retries):

1. Server "suplosmp" (a Minecraft Bedrock server, family "bedrock") — type "game update" — failing repeatedly over 19h, 13h, 11h, 5h, 2h, 1h, 48m, 37m ago (i.e. it keeps getting re-queued and keeps failing). Error message starts: "game update not verified: bedrock on suplosmp is \"inactive\" — your game server i..." (truncated in UI).

2. Server "projectzomboid-kc0kcr" (Project Zomboid) — type "game update" — same recurring pattern over the same time windows. Error: "game update not verified: projectzomboid on projectzomboid-kc0kcr is \"activating..." (truncated).

3. Server "cs2-dbhy4p" (a CS2 server, already known to have had disk-space issues fixed earlier) — type "provision" — one failure 5h ago. Error: "game port 27015/tcp never opened on 139.99.125.21:20048 after ~300s (31 attempt(..." (truncated).

I need you to investigate and report back, NOT fix anything yet (this is diagnostic only):

1. Find the actual code that creates/handles "game update" jobs — likely in worker/index.ts or a dedicated worker file (grep for "game update", "not verified", or similar). Read the FULL error message template/logic to understand exactly what "not verified" means and what status check it's doing (looks like it expects the game process to report a specific status like "active" but is finding "inactive" or "activating" instead).
2. Determine WHY this would recur indefinitely — is this a scheduled/cron job that re-triggers "game update" for these specific servers on a fixed interval? Check for a cron/scheduler that enqueues "game update" jobs (grep for job creation with type "game update" or similar, e.g. `db.job.create` with that type, or a cron entry).
3. Check the actual current status of these two servers in the DB (suplosmp and projectzomboid-kc0kcr) — are they actually running/healthy from the customer's perspective, or are they actually broken? Use appropriate DB query tooling available in the repo (there should be scripts or a documented way to query prod DB, check CLAUDE.md or existing scripts/tmp-*.mjs patterns used before in this codebase). Also check via SSH/docker on the actual host if you can determine which VM hosts these servers, whether the actual game process is running.
4. For cs2-dbhy4p specifically: check if this is a one-off transient failure or if the server is currently stuck/erroring in a provision loop. Check its current status in the DB.
5. Look at whether this "not verified" check is fundamentally a health-check/monitoring job (harmless retries, doesn't affect the live server) vs something that's blocking actual updates from applying, and whether the constant fail/retry cycle is generating noise/log spam or costing real resources.

Report back concisely: root cause of the recurring failures, whether customers are actually impacted (are the servers actually down), and what the cs2-dbhy4p provision failure means. Do not make any code or DB changes — this is read-only investigation. Keep the report under 400 words plus key code snippets/line refs.

179	        `  say "STEAM_RC:$rc"`,

182	        // there was. Both used to match one grep, so the two outcomes were

184	        `  if printf '%s' "$out" | grep -q "Success! App '${appId}' already up to date"; then`,

207	        // is disconnected, four times a day, forever, to change nothing. The
208	        // rule two paragraphs up applies here MOST, and used not to be applied

248	export type GameUpdateFacts = {
249	  /** The systemd unit the script acted on, or null when nothing matched. */
250	  unit: string | null;
251	  /** `systemctl is-active` before the restart. */
252	  wasActive: string;
253	  /** Exit code of `systemctl restart`, or null when it never ran. */
254	  restartRc: number | null;
255	  /** `systemctl is-active` after the restart, settled or timed out. */
256	  state: string;
257	  /**

259	   * was already up to date and downloaded nothing. Collapsing those two into one
260	   * value is what made "<game> updated on <host>" fire every 6 hours forever.
261	   */
262	  steam: "ok" | "current" | "failed" | "absent" | "na" | "unknown";
263	  steamRc: number | null;
264	  steamErrors: string[];
265	  /** Did the script run to completion? No END marker means we know nothing. */
266	  complete: boolean;
267	};

269	export function parseGameUpdateOutput(out: string): GameUpdateFacts {
270	  const text = String(out ?? "");
271	  const one = (re: RegExp): string | null => re.exec(text)?.[1] ?? null;
272	
273	  const steamRaw = one(/^NXGU:STEAM:(\w+)$/m);
274	  const steam =
275	    steamRaw === "OK" ? "ok"
276	    : steamRaw === "CURRENT" ? "current"
277	    : steamRaw === "FAIL" ? "failed"
278	    : steamRaw === "ABSENT" ? "absent"
279	    : steamRaw === "NA" ? "na"
280	    : "unknown";
281	
282	  const rc = (re: RegExp): number | null => {
283	    const v = one(re);
284	    return v === null ? null : Number(v);
285	  };
286	
287	  const unitLine = one(/^NXGU:UNIT:(.+)$/m);
288	  const steamErrors: string[] = [];
289	  for (const m of text.matchAll(/^NXGU:STEAM_ERR:(.*)$/gm)) steamErrors.push(m[1].trim());
290	
291	  return {
292	    unit: unitLine === null || unitLine === "NONE" ? null : unitLine.trim(),
293	    wasActive: one(/^NXGU:WAS:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
294	    restartRc: rc(/^NXGU:RESTART_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
295	    state: one(/^NXGU:STATE:(.*)$/m)?.trim() || "unknown",
296	    steam,
297	    steamRc: rc(/^NXGU:STEAM_RC:(-?\d+)$/m),
298	    steamErrors,
299	    complete: /^NXGU:END$/m.test(text),
300	  };

310	      title: string;
311	      body: string;
312	      /**
313	       * Is this an EVENT worth interrupting the customer for?
314	       *

317	       * outcome as not telling them"; the success path had no equivalent and
318	       * notified on every single pass, so a healthy server produced four
319	       * notifications a day, forever, all of them titled "<game> updated on
320	       * <host>" when nothing had been updated. Only a real, observed change is
321	       * an event.

335	 */

337	  family: GameFamily;
338	  hostname: string;
339	  facts: GameUpdateFacts;
340	}): GameUpdateVerdict {
341	  const { family, hostname, facts: f } = opts;
342	  const appId = STEAM_APPID[family];
343

346	      ok: false,
347	      reason:
348	        `the update script did not run to completion on ${hostname} (no end marker), so nothing about ` +
349	        `this run can be verified — the connection may have dropped or the command timed out. ` +

352	  }
353	
354	  if (!f.unit) {

358	        `no systemd service for ${family} was found on ${hostname}, so nothing was updated and ` +
359	        `nothing was restarted. Check what the server actually runs with: ` +
360	        `systemctl list-units --type=service | grep -i ${family}`,
361	    };
362	  }
363	
364	  if (appId && f.steam === "absent") {
365	    return {
366	      ok: false,
367	      reason:
368	        `steamcmd is not installed on ${hostname}, so the ${family} game files were NOT updated. ` +
369	        `Auto-update cannot work on this server until it is present: apt-get install -y steamcmd ` +
370	        `(or reinstall from the ${family} image).`,
371	    };
372	  }
373	
374	  if (appId && f.steam !== "ok" && f.steam !== "current") {
375	    const detail = f.steamErrors.length ? ` steamcmd said: ${f.steamErrors.slice(0, 3).join(" | ")}` : "";
376	    return {

378	      reason:
379	        `steamcmd did not report a successful update of app ${appId} on ${hostname} ` +
380	        `(exit ${f.steamRc ?? "unknown"}), so the game files were not updated and the service was ` +
381	        `left alone.${detail} Re-run by hand: steamcmd +login anonymous +app_update ${appId} validate +quit`,
382	    };
383	  }
384	
385	  // Nothing was restarted on these paths, so the state we observed is simply the
386	  // state the server was already in — do not describe it as a restart outcome.
387	  const restarted = f.steam === "ok";
388	
389	  if (f.state !== "active") {

392	      reason: restarted

395	          `, so your game server is NOT running. It was "${f.wasActive}" before this ran. ` +
396	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`
397	        : `${f.unit} on ${hostname} is "${f.state}" — your game server is NOT running. Nothing was ` +
398	          `updated or restarted by this check, so this is not something we just did to it. ` +
399	          `Diagnose with: systemctl status ${f.unit} ; journalctl -u ${f.unit} -n 50`,
400	    };
401	  }
402	
403	  if (f.steam === "ok") {
404	    return {
405	      ok: true,
406	      notify: true, // a new build really was downloaded and applied
407	      title: `${family} updated on ${hostname}`,
408	      body:
409	        `steamcmd downloaded a new build of app ${appId}, and ${f.unit} was restarted and is active again ` +
410	        `(verified with systemctl, not assumed from an exit code).`,
411	    };
412	  }
413	
414	  if (f.steam === "current") {
415	    return {
416	      ok: true,
417	      notify: false, // nothing happened; four of these a day is noise, not news
418	      title: `${family} on ${hostname} is already up to date`,
419	      body:
420	        `steamcmd confirmed app ${appId} is already up to date, so nothing was downloaded and ${f.unit} was ` +
421	        `NOT restarted — no players were disconnected. It is active.`,
422	    };
423	  }
424	
425	  // No update source exists for this family. Say that, rather than implying one —
426	  // and do not restart, which is all this job could otherwise do here.

428	    ok: true,
429	    notify: false,
